name: Castlethorpe First School

areas.summary: Strong publicly visible evidence for curriculum (8 specific items). Themes include ambitious, balanced, broad, curriculum.

signals.text: During periods of remote learning, children will receive a planned programme of activities focused on core areas of learning, including reading, writing, phonics and maths, alongside opportunities for creativity and physical activity.
Built around rich thematic learning, the curriculum enables children to make meaningful connections across subjects while developing knowledge, skills, and understanding progressively over time.

KS1 Curriculum Village Schools Federation Long Term Curriculum Overview Our Key Stage 1 long-term curriculum overview is organised through a carefully structured two-year cycle, designed to provide a broad, balanced, and engaging curriculum for all pupils, including those within mixed-age classes.
Overall, the curriculum reflects a thoughtful and ambitious approach that combines academic achievement with creativity, personal development, and cultural understanding.
Skills are carefully sequenced so that learning builds progressively over time, allowing children to develop confidence, independence and deeper understanding.

areas.narrativeSummary: During periods of remote learning, children will receive a planned programme of activities focused on core areas of learning, including reading, writing, phonics and maths, alongside opportunities for creativity and physical activity.

areas.summary: Limited public evidence for enrichment and extra-curricular activity (1 excerpt; mostly general statements rather than specific provision).

signals.text: The clubs provide a variety of toys, games, activities, arts and crafts and outside play.

areas.narrativeSummary: The school mentions The clubs provide a variety of toys, games, activities, arts and crafts and outside play.. See the source link below for the original page.

areas.summary: Strong publicly visible evidence for ethos and values (6 specific items). Themes include belong, community, happy, inclusive.

signals.text: Our children learn in happy, exciting, respectful and supportive environments, providing them with the knowledge and cultural capital needed to succeed in life.
Our children learn in happy, exciting, respectful, and supportive environments, equipping them with the knowledge and cultural capital necessary for success in life.
RE introduces children to different beliefs, values, and traditions, helping foster respect and understanding of diversity.

There is a shared expectation that all pupils, regardless of their specific needs, should receive inclusive teaching that facilitates optimal progress and fosters a sense of belonging within the wider school community.

areas.narrativeSummary: Our children learn in happy, exciting, respectful and supportive environments, providing them with the knowledge and cultural capital needed to succeed in life.

areas.summary: Little public evidence found about behaviour and pastoral care from scanned sources.
areas.narrativeSummary: We did not find much about behaviour & pastoral care on the pages and documents scanned for this school. Worth asking on a visit or checking the school's website directly.

areas.summary: Strong publicly visible evidence for SEND and inclusion (10 specific items). Themes include access, inclusion, inclusive, individual.

signals.text: Teachers use the Skills Progression document to inform their weekly and daily planning, ensuring that activities are purposeful, developmentally appropriate and tailored to meet the needs of individual children.
Our SEND provision is designed to ensure that all pupils, regardless of their needs, feel included, valued, and able to reach their full potential.
Additionally, the Local Authority’s local offer is to enable parents and young people to see more clearly what services are available, communicating their provision for SEND.
Furthermore, the Local Authority’s local offer effectively communicates the services available to parents and young people, ensuring clarity in our provision for SEND.

areas.narrativeSummary: Teachers use the Skills Progression document to inform their weekly and daily planning, ensuring that activities are purposeful, developmentally appropriate and tailored to meet the needs of individual children.

areas.summary: Moderate publicly visible evidence for community and parental engagement (4 specific items). Themes include community, families, local, parents.

signals.text: Forest School aims to foster a relationship with nature through regular personal experiences in order to develop long-term, environmentally sustainable attitudes and practices in staff, children and the wider community.
Additionally, the Local Authority’s local offer is to enable parents and young people to see more clearly what services are available, communicating their provision for SEND.
Furthermore, the Local Authority’s local offer effectively communicates the services available to parents and young people, ensuring clarity in our provision for SEND.
By working together with families, we aim to ensure every child continues to flourish, wherever they are learning.

areas.narrativeSummary: Forest School aims to foster a relationship with nature through regular personal experiences in order to develop long-term, environmentally sustainable attitudes and practices in staff, children and the wider community.

Cookie Policy

SEND
Special Educational Need and Disability
At Castlethorpe First School, provision for pupils with SEND is co-ordinated by the Village Schools Federation SENDCo Mrs Adey Underwood (Inclusion Lead).
Contact: senco@villageschoolsfederation.co.uk
At Castlethorpe First School, we believe that every pupil deserves the support they need to thrive. Our SEND provision is designed to ensure that all pupils, regardless of their needs, feel included, valued, and able to reach their full potential. Our aim is to make sure that every pupil gets the right support, at the right time. We know that parents and carers are key partners in their child’s education and that is why we are here to listen to your concerns, answer your questions, and work with you every step of the way. At Stoke Goldington CE School, inclusion is at the heart of what we do and we strive to create a school where all pupils can feel safe, make friends, and enjoy learning—no matter their starting point or the challenges they face. Together, we can help every pupil shine.
As an inclusive school, we offer a range of provisions tailored to support children with various Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND), including those with social, communication, and interaction needs, learning difficulties, emotional and mental health needs, and physical needs.
We endeavour to promptly identify each child’s particular needs and respond appropriately, enabling them to make progress alongside their peers. Stoke Goldington CE School is committed to providing an inclusive, quality education to all pupils across our family of schools, promoting equality of access and opportunity in all areas of the curriculum. Our children learn in happy, exciting, respectful, and supportive environments, equipping them with the knowledge and cultural capital necessary for success in life.
There is a shared expectation that all pupils, regardless of their specific needs, should receive inclusive teaching that facilitates optimal progress and fosters a sense of belonging within the wider school community. The Village Federation Schools (VSF) implements a systematic approach to ensure continuity of provision, aligned with the Government’s SEND Code of Practice (2014) and our SEN Policy. Furthermore, the Local Authority’s local offer effectively communicates the services available to parents and young people, ensuring clarity in our provision for SEND.

EYFS Curriculum
Village Schools Federation EYFS Skills Progression
Our EYFS Skills Progression document supports high-quality teaching and learning throughout the Early Years Foundation Stage. It is designed to ensure that children develop the essential knowledge, skills and behaviours needed for future success through carefully planned, progressive learning experiences.
The document identifies the key skills children will work towards across all areas of learning, including communication and language, personal, social and emotional development, physical development, literacy, mathematics and understanding the world. Skills are carefully sequenced so that learning builds progressively over time, allowing children to develop confidence, independence and deeper understanding.
Teachers use the Skills Progression document to inform their weekly and daily planning, ensuring that activities are purposeful, developmentally appropriate and tailored to meet the needs of individual children. It helps staff identify what children need to learn next and supports consistent expectations across the EYFS.
The document also ensures a balance between adult-directed teaching and child-initiated learning. Through high-quality interactions, play-based experiences and carefully planned environments, children are given opportunities to practise and apply their developing skills in meaningful contexts.
Our EYFS Skills Progression document is firmly rooted in the Early Years Foundation Stage Framework and reflects our commitment to providing a nurturing, ambitious and engaging curriculum that supports every child to thrive.

KS1 Curriculum
Village Schools Federation Long Term Curriculum Overview
Our Key Stage 1 long-term curriculum overview is organised through a carefully structured two-year cycle, designed to provide a broad, balanced, and engaging curriculum for all pupils, including those within mixed-age classes. Built around rich thematic learning, the curriculum enables children to make meaningful connections across subjects while developing knowledge, skills, and understanding progressively over time.
The cyclical structure of Cycle A and Cycle B ensures full curriculum coverage without unnecessary repetition, allowing pupils to experience a diverse range of increasingly challenging learning opportunities as they move through Key Stage 1. Overall, the curriculum reflects a thoughtful and ambitious approach that combines academic achievement with creativity, personal development, and cultural understanding. It is designed to make learning immersive, connected, and relevant, fostering curiosity about themselves, their communities, and the wider world.
The academic year is divided into three overarching thematic strands: People and Communities, Buildings and Places, and The Natural World. Each strand is explored across the autumn, spring, and summer terms through memorable and child-centred topics. In Cycle A, for example, pupils begin by exploring personal identity and community through topics such as This is Me! and Respect Our World. During the spring term, the focus shifts toward history and geography-based learning through themes like My City and Castles. In the summer term, the curriculum broadens children’s understanding of global diversity and environments with topics such as Where is Africa? and Life in Africa.
The curriculum is deliberately cross-curricular.
English is closely linked to each topic, allowing pupils to develop writing and reading skills through purposeful contexts. This approach ensures literacy skills are embedded authentically within the wider curriculum rather than taught in isolation.
Mathematics follows a progressive mastery model, with both Year 1 and Year 2 objectives carefully mapped throughout the year. Key mathematical concepts such as place value, addition and subtraction, multiplication and division, fractions, measurement, geometry, and statistics are revisited and developed incrementally. The structure demonstrates clear progression while ensuring opportunities for consolidation and application.
Science learning is similarly sequenced to build children’s understanding of the natural and physical world. The curriculum promotes enquiry, observation, investigation, and scientific vocabulary development, helping children become increasingly curious and analytical learners.
Foundation subjects are integrated meaningfully into each termly theme. Computing lessons develop digital literacy and programming skills alongside safe and responsible technology use. History and geography are taught through engaging contexts that encourage children to understand chronology, place, culture, and human impact on the environment. Art and Design Technology provide opportunities for creativity, evaluation, problem-solving, and technical skill development through practical projects linked to each topic.
The curriculum also places significant emphasis on pupils’ personal development. PSHER supports emotional wellbeing, relationships, responsibility, and citizenship. RE introduces children to different beliefs, values, and traditions, helping foster respect and understanding of diversity. Music and PE contribute to children’s creative expression, confidence, teamwork, coordination, and physical health.

Forest School
"The principles of forest schools foster a holistic form of education that encourages children to connect deeply with nature, embrace risk and challenges, and grow into confident, environmentally aware individuals. These principles are essential for cultivating a future generation that values both personal growth and ecological sustainability." Forest School Association
Our Forest School sessions happen every week throughout the 3 years the children are with us, through all the seasons. We try to create a Forest School community where we are each connected to nature and to each other. Our sessions usually start with some social games to get us in the mood; we then move on to the "topic" for that week as well as all the usual activities. The sessions are child-led, and we explore the world through their interests and curiosity.
Through our activities we hope to be able to understand and appreciate the natural environment. We focus on weekly identification skills, getting to really know our environment so that we can observe the differences throughout the year. We use fire to celebrate special events, focusing on fire safety and cooking naturally resourced products. We use knives and peelers under supervision to encourage motor skills, concentration and support risk assessing.
We use rope swings to improve balance, upper arm strength and emotional regulation. Climbing trees, exploring the physical feel of the site is incredibly important to brain and muscle development.
Forest School aims to foster a relationship with nature through regular personal experiences in order to develop long-term, environmentally sustainable attitudes and practices in staff, children and the wider community. We focus heavily on the good practice of caring for our environment and the wider world and how we can support any challenges it may be facing.
To sum it up: we aim to develop, where appropriate, the physical, social, cognitive, linguistic, emotional and spiritual aspects of our children.

pageCache.text:
Looked After Children
At Castlethorpe First School, we are committed to fostering a whole school culture that prioritises the personalised learning needs of Looked After Children (LAC) and Previously Looked After Children (PLAC). We recognise that these pupils require tailored support to address their personal, emotional, and academic needs effectively.
Looked After Children (LAC) are defined as those who are in the care of a Local Authority (LA) or provided with accommodation by the LA for a continuous period exceeding 24 hours. Previously Looked After Children (PLAC) are those who have transitioned from care due to a child arrangements order, a special guardianship order, or an adoption order.
We strive to work collaboratively with families, social workers, and the Virtual School to create an environment that emphasises stability, safety, and individual care. This partnership is essential in ensuring that LAC and PLAC receive the attention and support necessary for their holistic development.
Cookie Policy

Remote Education
At The Village Schools Federation, we are committed to ensuring that all children continue to feel supported, connected and inspired in their learning when learning from home. Our remote education offer provides high-quality learning experiences that help children continue to make progress and maintain a strong sense of belonging.
During periods of remote learning, children will receive a planned programme of activities focused on core areas of learning, including reading, writing, phonics and maths, alongside opportunities for creativity and physical activity.
Children may access a mixture of:
Live or recorded lessons
Online activities and resources
Story sessions and collective worship/ assembly
Regular contact with staff through Teams or Class Dojo
We are committed to supporting all pupils, including those with additional needs, through adapted activities and regular communication with families.
Safeguarding and online safety remain a priority at all times, and all remote learning is delivered in line with the school’s safeguarding and data protection procedures.
By working together with families, we aim to ensure every child continues to flourish, wherever they are learning.
Cookie Policy

School Closures
In the event of an unplanned school closure, every effort will be made to inform parents and carers as quickly as possible using ParentMail.
We strongly encourage all families to ensure their contact details are kept up to date and that notifications from ParentMail are enabled, so important messages can be received promptly.
